oneLine: Money you keep aside only for surprises, like losing your job.
explanation: An emergency fund is money you save for costs you did not plan. It is not for holidays or shopping.
Many people keep it in a savings account. They can take the money out quickly when they need it.
A common goal is three to six months of living costs.
whyItMatters: Without an emergency fund, a surprise bill can push you into debt. Debt on a credit card often has a high APR. With a fund, you can pay the bill and keep your plans.
workedExample: Your living costs are $2,000 a month. Three months of costs is $6,000. You save $250 each month. After 24 months, the fund holds $6,000.

sources.name: CFPB, An essential guide to building an emergency fund
